quickStart.item_07: For a police emergency in South Korea call 112; for fire or ambulance call 119.
quickStart.item_15: For healthcare, confirm your National Health Insurance status and whether your My Number Card is registered as the health-insurance certificate or an eligibility document is available.
quickStart.item_56: Review emergency contacts, health information, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, investments, pensions, and essential liabilities.
quickStart.item_28: If someone has died, contact the municipal office, health insurer, National Pension Service, financial institutions, employer, and tax office as relevant.
quickStart.item_43: Keep the export encrypted. Never put RRN credentials, My Number Card PINs, e-Tax credentials, passwords, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes.item_116: The 12-digit My Number is assigned to people with a resident record in Japan; the Individual Number Card is a separate card. Do not treat the identifier, physical card, and card PIN as interchangeable.
legalNotes.item_119: The Digital Agency states that new health insurance certificates stopped being issued from December 2, 2024. Existing certificates remained valid until expiry, up to December 1, 2025; current arrangements use a registered My Number Card or an insurer-issued eligibility certificate as applicable. Confirm with the insurer.
legalNotes.item_44: Japan's National Pension and Employees' Pension Insurance have separate enrollment and benefit rules. Survivor benefits depend on contribution history and eligibility.
legalNotes.item_38: Inheritance tax may apply depending on the estate, heirs, residence, and other circumstances. NTA filing and payment requirements can include time limits; confirm current rules and advice for the specific estate.
legalNotes.item_04: Adult guardianship, voluntary guardianship, wills, and private powers of attorney have different legal effects. Confirm formal requirements with the relevant Family Court, a notary, or a qualified Japanese lawyer.
legalNotes.item_83: Official: Japan pension systems and survivor benefits: https://www.nenkin.go.jp/international/english/japanese-system/index.html
legalNotes.item_20: Emergency numbers: Japan National Tourism Organization: https://www.japan.travel/en/plan/

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in Japan. Confirm representative authority and current municipal, pension, court, and tax requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Japan
meta.reviewedBy: Government sources reviewed; case-specific legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Follow municipal death-registration instructions, identify the executor or representative, notify relevant insurers and providers, and keep a record of each action.

startHere.0: Follow the municipal death-registration and resident-record procedures that apply to the circumstances.
startHere.1: Locate the will and identify the executor; seek advice if there is no will or the estate is complex.
startHere.2: Contact the health insurer, Japan Pension Service, banks, employer, insurers, and tax office as relevant.
startHere.3: List assets, debts, regular payments, and claims; confirm authority and obligations before changing payments or distributing property.
startHere.4: Keep a log of contacts, forms, and documents supplied. Never use the deceased person's My Number Card PIN or online credentials.

legalFramework.1: Japan National Pension and Employees' Pension Insurance survivor-benefit rules.
legalFramework.2: National Tax Agency inheritance-tax and final income-tax rules.
legalFramework.3: Family Court adult guardianship procedures and relevant notarial instruments.
legalFramework.4: Bank, insurer, property, and investment-provider processes.

2.focus: Complete required court, tax, property, and provider procedures before final distribution.

3.focus: Review the surviving household's will, guardianship, pension, health-insurance, and secure-record arrangements.
